sugestoes.texto: WHAT: readSequence() does not verify that each element fits inside the sequence's declared content length, and readLength() silently returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding. WHY: A malformed DER ECDSA signature supplied from a JWT can be parsed even though it violates DER rules, potentially producing an accepted concatenated r|s signature. HOW: In readSequence(), throw IOException if bytes.length > length before subtracting; in readLength(), throw IOException for length == 0x80 instead of returning -1.

issues.descricao: Claims getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider instead of BouncyCastle; that is the intended fallback for the BC-free authz client.
Claims readLength's -1 for indefinite-length encoding breaks length arithmetic or array allocation; the decoder only parses locally generated DER and the sequence path already rejects it.
Claims the lenient sequence parser allows malformed or trailing DER and signature malleability in verification; the parser never sees external signatures.
Claims integerToBytes can silently truncate oversized INTEGER values; inputs come from local signing and always fit the component width.
Claims createECParams/getKeyFactory throwing UnsupportedOperationException breaks EC JWK parsing in the authz client; the client does not use that path.

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes the -1 returned by readLength for indefinite-length encoding to read(int), which allocates new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of an IOException on malformed DER input.
integerToBytes silently truncates r/s values longer than the curve size, so non-canonical DER signatures are accepted as different values (signature malleability).
AuthzClient.create eagerly initializes CryptoIntegration, so a shaded/repackaged client that lost its ServiceLoader file fails at construction instead of only when ECDSA is used.

Calling CryptoIntegration.init from AuthzClient.create is claimed to lock the global crypto provider to the minimal AuthzClientCryptoProvider so a later server init is ignored and unsupported operations fail.
The ignored-providers message is passed to logger.debugf as a format string instead of using logger.debug, and keeps a trailing comma.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: the new login cache is not invalidated when an organization is disabled or deleted. WHY: `InfinispanOrganizationProvider.registerOrganizationInvalidation` only invalidates org-specific keys, so `getForLogin` can return stale internal IDs for org-bound public IDPs after the organization becomes unavailable. HOW: in `InfinispanOrganizationProvider.registerOrganizationInvalidation`, also call `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode))` for every `FetchMode` whenever an organization changes.

WHAT: the cached `getForLogin` path resolves each IDP with a separate `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` call. WHY: when the per-IDP cache is cold (e.g., after invalidation), a realm with N login IDPs triggers N+1 database round-trips on a login hot path. HOW: store full `IdentityProviderModel` objects in `IdentityProviderListQuery` instead of only internal IDs, or add a batch `getByIds(Collection<String>)` lookup so the list can be hydrated in one query.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.
Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.
Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.
Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.
Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.
Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.
Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

getForLogin caches all organizations under one realm/mode entry, so each new organizationId invalidates and rebuilds that entry with every previously cached search merged in, instead of caching per organization.

Disabling an organization does not invalidate the cached login IDP lists in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin, so callers that do not re-check isEnabled could get IDPs of a disabled organization.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The emailMatch property rejects any email stored in rejectedEmails before checking whether the OAuth provider already validated it via authOptions. WHY: A user whose email failed a previous manual signup cannot complete OAuth signup with the same email because the client disables submit from stale cache, even though the server trusts the OAuth provider. HOW: Move the rejectedEmails.contains(email) check below the authOptions.email_valid branch so OAuth-validated emails take precedence.

issues.descricao: Claims the rejected-email memory stores the server-normalised email, so it never matches the raw input on retry.
Claims the 'rejectedEmails.@each' dependent key does not observe pushes of plain strings, so the rejection is not shown until the email changes.
BlockedEmail.should_block? returns nil instead of false when the email has no record.
Claims EmailValidator dropped the email format check that the old User#email_validator performed, allowing invalid emails.
Claims EmailValidator#email_in_restriction_setting? raises NoMethodError when the email is nil.
Claims the blocked-email validator specs would still pass if the blocked-email branch were removed.

`rejectedEmails` is declared as an array literal on the controller prototype, so it is shared across instances and modal sessions; emails rejected once keep failing validation later. Initialize it per instance in `init`.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The `CalendarEvent` built for `sendAddGuestsEmails` never includes a `team` property. WHY: `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates over `calendarEvent.team?.members`, but that branch is always undefined here, so co-hosts on team/collective bookings are silently skipped when new guests are added. HOW: Include `eventType.team.members` when fetching the booking and populate `evt.team`, or remove the dead loop if team notifications are not intended.

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.
Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.
sendAddGuestsEmails never notifies the newly added guests because the formatted event does not contain them, so the newGuests branch is unreachable.
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail reads calEvent.attendees[0].name without a guard and throws when the attendee list is empty.
The AddGuests dialog error toast shows the raw server error message and code, which could display internal backend details such as Prisma errors to the user.
Swallowing email-sending errors returns success even if notification emails fail; the failure should be surfaced to the UI.
Claims the organizer add-guests email subject uses attendees[0].name, which becomes empty because newly added guests are stored with an empty name.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: PropertyResourceBundle is loaded from FileInputStream, which Java specifies as ISO-8859-1, while the theme message properties files are UTF-8 encoded. WHY: Non-ASCII characters in translations (Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic, etc.) are corrupted before sanitization, producing garbled diagnostic output and undermining the verifier's reliability on non-English files. HOW: Open the files with a UTF-8 Reader, e.g., `new PropertyResourceBundle(Files.newBufferedReader(file.toPath(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.
Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.
Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.
VerifyMessageProperties loads message bundles with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), claimed to decode as ISO-8859-1 and produce mojibake and spurious Illegal HTML failures for non-English files.
The message verifier compares English files against themselves, so any anchor tag in an English source, including an unsafe href, is stripped before the HTML sanitizer check and never reported.
Error messages in the verifier include absolute file paths; the comment states no data-exposure defect was found.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `createInitialDeployment` enables the `rolling-updates` feature only when `updateStrategy` is non-null. WHY: The parameterized test runs with `null` and `RECREATE`, so the null-strategy case deploys Keycloak without enabling the preview feature, which the updated docs say causes the operator to fail during preview update handling. HOW: Move the `FeatureSpec` creation and `setEnabledFeatures` call before the `if (updateStrategy == null) return kc;` branch so every test case enables the feature.

issues.descricao: Claims the rolling-updates feature is not enabled for the null update strategy in UpgradeTest, so that case tests the operator without the gated feature.
Claims RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3 and 4 now means feature disabled, a breaking change that needs release notes.
Claims calling picocli.exit() for the disabled-feature exit code is incorrect because it calls System.exit directly.
Claims `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` in UpdateCompatibilityCheck can hit a null profile and throw NullPointerException because initProfile is skipped for update-compatibility.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The override timezone conversion uses override.start.toString() to feed dayjs.tz, so the parsed wall-clock time depends on the Node.js process timezone. WHY: On a server not running UTC, the same override produces different availability boundaries and can shift or drop slots. HOW: Parse the stored UTC Date's wall-clock explicitly with dayjs.utc(override.start).format(...) before interpreting it in the organizer timezone.

WHAT: The activeOverrides filter keeps only overrides whose UTC start timestamp falls within the invitee's day. WHY: When the organizer is in a timezone ahead of the invitee, an override for the organizer's local day can start on the previous UTC day but still overlap the invitee's day, so the override is discarded and slots are missing. HOW: Replace the start-point check with an interval-overlap check against the invitee day.

issues.descricao: Claims checkIfIsAvailable interprets date overrides in organizerTimeZone instead of each override owner's timezone.
The new different-timezone date-override test expects the same UTC slots as the existing case and would still pass if the offset fix in slots.ts were reverted.
Claims the selected-slots availability call site passes only the user's timezone, so dateOverrides and workingHours fall back to [] and slots are checked only against busy times.
Claims getSlots uses the optional override.timeZone, so an override without it passes undefined to dayjs.tz and computes a wrong offset using the server timezone.
checkIfIsAvailable calls dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone) guarded only by truthiness, so an invalid time-zone string would throw and abort getSchedule.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected() == 0, but on SQLite a matching UPDATE that sets identical values reports zero rows changed. WHY: When the device limit is reached, a legitimate existing device can be rejected if its client_ip, user_agent and updated_at are unchanged, because the code cannot distinguish 'row not found' from 'row matched but not modified'. HOW: When RowsAffected is 0, run a SELECT for device_id in the active window and only return ErrDeviceLimitReached if the device is absent.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.
Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.
Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.
Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
ProvideAnonDBStore gained an int64 deviceLimit parameter but is still registered as a wire provider in pkg/server/wire.go, which has no provider for int64, so wire generation or compilation fails.

ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an int64 deviceLimit but is still registered as a Wire provider (with an AnonStore bind) in pkg/server/wire.go; Wire cannot supply an int64, so DI generation and the server build fail.
Claims updateDevice's RowsAffected()==0 check wrongly denies already-registered devices on MySQL because MySQL reports changed rather than matched rows.
CreateOrUpdateDevice runs a full COUNT over the 30-day anon_device table on every anonymous request when a device limit is set.
The 'device limit reached' error string is hard-coded English and bypasses i18n.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The per-resource permission-denial cache is consulted before the permission cache and is never invalidated when a fresh permission lookup succeeds. WHY: If a user was previously denied for a resource, the cached denial can persist and prevent the new requery path from seeing a later grant, causing false denials until the denial-cache TTL expires. HOW: Delete the matching denial-cache entry when a fresh database lookup returns allowed, or reconsider caching denials at the individual resource level.

WHAT: `Check` writes a denial-cache entry keyed partly by user-supplied `Name` and `ParentFolder` for every database deny, with no size or rate limit. WHY: Each distinct failed resource check creates a new cache entry that lives for the denial-cache TTL, so an enumeration of names can grow the in-process cache unboundedly and consume memory. HOW: Bound the denial cache with a max-entry/LRU limit or avoid per-resource negative caching.

WHAT: The per-resource denial cache is consulted before the permission cache and is never invalidated when permissions are updated. WHY: A Check that previously denied a resource stores a denial entry for 30s; if the user is subsequently granted permission, every Check for that exact resource returns false until the TTL expires, contradicting the PR goal of allowing access to newly created dashboards/folders. HOW: Invalidate the user's denial-cache entries when getIdentityPermissions refreshes the permission cache, or skip the denial cache when the positive permission cache is stale/missing so the DB is requeried.

issues.descricao: Claims a cached denial blocks access granted within the TTL window; denials are TTL-bounded like the existing permission cache.
Claims trusting cached grants while re-checking cached denials lets stale grants keep access to revoked resources; cached grants were already served for the TTL before this PR.
Claims per-resource denial entries cause unbounded cache memory growth; entries expire after the short TTL.
Claims List now serves stale cached permissions whereas it previously always queried the DB; List was already cache-backed before the change.

Claims the new denial cache is checked before any permission source and never invalidated, so a Check that ran before a resource was created or a grant was added keeps returning Allowed:false for the whole short cache TTL.
Claims the remote authz client still wraps results in a 30s LocalCache, so in remote deployments new dashboards, folders and grants stay invisible for up to 30s.
Claims permissionCacheUsage counts a cache hit that did not grant access as a cache miss.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The cron query that finds cancelled reminders to cancel against SendGrid does not restrict results to email reminders. WHY: It then posts to /v3/user/scheduled_sends using reminder.referenceId as batch_id; if an SMS WorkflowReminder ever carried cancelled: true, an SMS reference would be sent to SendGrid, causing incorrect cancellations and errors. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` to the where clause of remindersToCancel.

issues.descricao: The booking-page reschedule path cancels email reminders with immediateDelete=true, which leaves the WorkflowReminder row in the DB, while the dashboard reschedule path marks it cancelled for cleanup, so the two flows are inconsistent.
Claims the code comment overstates the cancel window because the query lacks a lower bound on scheduledDate.
Claims the cron's cancel loop uses an undefined `client` variable, causing a ReferenceError.
Claims the unscheduled-reminders query re-schedules reminders marked cancelled because it lacks a cancelled filter.
Claims a hard-coded "Verification code" placeholder bypasses i18n.
Claims a hard-coded "Verify" button label bypasses i18n.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid send but neither deletes nor marks the WorkflowReminder row, leaving orphaned scheduled rows inconsistent with the non-immediate path.
Claims reminders from disabled event types are still sent and can be re-scheduled because they are only marked cancelled.
Notes the isSenderIdNeeded branch removal without reporting a problem.
The new cancelled column is nullable without a default, so existing WorkflowReminder rows get null instead of false.

With immediateDelete=true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row, and the callers no longer delete it, so reminder rows are left orphaned in the database.
The reschedule path cancels SendGrid email reminders immediately (immediateDelete=true) instead of flagging them cancelled for the cron, which supposedly accumulates cancelled batches.
When an email reminder is cancelled immediately on reschedule, its WorkflowReminder row is never deleted or marked cancelled, so stale scheduled reminder rows are left in the database.
Claims the cron's cancelled-reminders query can pick rows with a null referenceId and send batch_id:null to SendGrid, aborting cancellation of the remaining reminders.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The goroutines performing best-effort legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection have no panic recovery. WHY: A panic inside any legacy storage implementation crashes the entire Grafana process instead of being contained like the other best-effort errors. HOW: Wrap each goroutine body with `defer func() { if r := recover(); r != nil { log.Error(fmt.Errorf("%v", r), "panic in legacy write") } }()`.

issues.descricao: Claims the Equal/NotEqual assertions in the Mode 3 tests can never fail, though the Equal assertion does fail if Delete stops returning the storage result.
Claims the legacy-create goroutine races with the caller on a shared obj that can alias the returned object.
Empty comment.
Every mode-3 write spawns an unbounded goroutine for the legacy store, risking goroutine and memory growth under load.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The template ends its if/else block with `<%- end if %>`, which is invalid Ruby/ERB syntax. WHY: Rendering the embed page raises a SyntaxError because Ruby does not have an `end if` block terminator. HOW: Close the block with `<%- end %>`.

WHAT: TopicEmbed.import_remote passes the URL straight to Kernel#open before any scheme validation. WHY: A URL starting with '|' executes a shell command and file:// URLs read local files; the Disqus import task calls this method directly with attacker-controlled XML links, enabling command injection and local file disclosure. HOW: Validate `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` before calling open, or use Net::HTTP with an explicit HTTP/HTTPS allowlist.

WHAT: PollFeed opens the configured feed URL with Kernel#open without validating the scheme. WHY: If an attacker can change feed_polling_url, values like '|cmd' execute arbitrary commands and file:// URLs disclose local files. HOW: Reject any URL that does not start with http:// or https:// before opening it.

WHAT: request.referer is interpolated directly into a JavaScript string without escaping. WHY: A referer containing single quotes or other JS metacharacters breaks the postMessage call and can inject arbitrary script into the embed iframe. HOW: Escape the value with escape_javascript (the `j` helper), e.g. `<%= j request.referer.to_s %>`.

WHAT: embed.js calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)` without verifying that `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` returned an element. WHY: If the host page loads the script but omits the target div, `comments` is null and `appendChild` throws a TypeError, breaking the page. HOW: Return early when the element is missing.

WHAT: fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without first checking whether the setting is present. WHY: When feed polling is disabled (the default) and embed_by_username is nil, retrieving a remote embed raises NoMethodError and the job fails instead of exiting cleanly. HOW: Return early if SiteSetting.embed_by_username.blank?, matching the guard in Jobs::PollFeed#execute.

issues.descricao: Claims embed.js throws a TypeError when the page lacks the #discourse-comments element because comments.appendChild is called on null.
Claims the embed controller spec fails because EmbedController#best only enqueues a Sidekiq job and never constructs TopicRetriever during the request.
The hourly PollFeed job always fetches and processes the full feed without a conditional GET; the feed_key helper meant for that is defined but never used.
States that the link fallback in PollFeed is correct; no problem is reported.
States the raw_html cook_method comparison in Post#cook is safe; no problem is reported.
States the cook_method assignment in PostCreator is correct; no problem is reported.
States the `if topic_id` check in EmbedController is safe; no problem is reported.
Describes the host checks in ensure_embeddable without reporting a problem.
States content_sha1 and absolutize_urls in TopicEmbed are correct; no problem is reported.
States the TopicRetriever throttle uses setnx and an explicit no_throttle check; no problem is reported.
Claims import_remote passes an unvalidated user-supplied URL to Kernel#open, allowing command execution with '|' or local file reads.
Claims PollFeed fetches SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validation, letting whoever controls that setting make the server request arbitrary internal or external URLs.
Claims the embed best.html.erb template closes its if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby, so every render raises a SyntaxError.
The embed layout interpolates request.referer into an inline JavaScript string with only HTML escaping, so a referer containing a quote can break out of the string and run script.
Claims postMessage drops the resize message because targetOrigin is the full referer URL rather than just the origin, breaking iframe auto-resize.
Claims setting X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL on the embed endpoint disables clickjacking protection and that the referer check can be spoofed.
Claims the cook_method migration default of 1 equals raw_html, so every post would skip cooking and sanitization.
Claims the 'not a url' TopicRetriever spec passes regardless of the InvalidURIError rescue because embeddable_host is blank.
`<%- end if %>` in embed/best.html.erb is not valid Ruby, so the template raises a SyntaxError and the embed page fails to render.
Claims `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling if modifier that makes the logo output the condition, so the logo renders before the header button.
Claims the embed best action builds the view for current_user and then marks it publicly cacheable, so a staff member's view could be served to anonymous visitors.
fetch_http calls SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase without a presence check, raising NoMethodError when the setting is blank.
poll_feed opens the feed URL without a timeout and imports every item without a cap, so a slow or huge feed can tie up a worker.
The TopicRetriever specs mock perform_retrieve, so a bug in invalid_host? would not make them fail.
The EmbedController success tests only assert that mocks are called and would pass even if the controller logic were removed.
poll_feed has no test of feed parsing or TopicEmbed.import; the specs only check the execute guards.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `AssignmentSource.from_dict` silently returns `None` when the dict has been serialized as JSON because `queued` arrives as an ISO-8601 string while the dataclass expects a `datetime`. WHY: Sentry's JSON encoder converts `datetime` objects to strings, so a dict produced by `to_dict()` cannot be reconstructed by `from_dict()`; the resulting `None` causes `should_sync` to skip the source-integration guard and the assignee sync cycle continues. HOW: Serialize only the fields required for cycle prevention in `to_dict` and reconstruct from those same fields in `from_dict`; if `queued` is needed later, parse the ISO string back to `datetime` in `from_dict`.

issues.descricao: Claims to_dict() returns a raw datetime for queued that fails JSON serialization when passed as Celery task kwargs.
The assignment_source parameter was added to the abstract sync_status_outbound instead of sync_assignee_outbound, which is the method that actually receives it.
Claims concrete integrations overriding should_sync(self, attribute) will raise TypeError at the new two-argument call in sync_assignee_outbound.
Claims a malformed assignment_source_dict makes from_dict return None, so should_sync fails open and re-enables the sync cycle.
test_to_dict asserts queued is not None, which is always true because queued has a default, so the assertion verifies nothing.
Claims passing AssignmentSource.to_dict() with a raw datetime to sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async fails Sentry's bad-pickle check in tests and would break under a JSON serializer.

sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that is never threaded through the status task or checked in should_sync, so status sync gets no cycle prevention despite the signature suggesting it.
The base sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter but ExampleIntegration's override takes no **kwargs, so callers passing assignment_source would raise TypeError.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join ignores the timeout argument required by the ProcessingStrategy contract and unconditionally calls close(). WHY: Arroyo's StreamProcessor calls close() then join(timeout) during shutdown; ignoring timeout means shutdown deadlines are not respected and close() runs a second time from inside join(), making the API contract unreliable. HOW: Implement join() to wait on the queue pool and commit thread respecting the supplied timeout, or at minimum pass timeout through to the underlying join calls instead of calling close().

WHAT: FixedQueuePool.shutdown joins each worker thread sequentially with a 5 s timeout per worker. WHY: With the default 20 queues, a shutdown where multiple workers are stuck on slow database calls can take up to 100 s before the pool returns, exceeding typical consumer shutdown deadlines and delaying process exit. HOW: Join workers concurrently (e.g., with threading.Condition or a single join with a shared deadline) so the whole pool shuts down in roughly one timeout period instead of num_queues * timeout.

WHAT: ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown calls FixedQueuePool.shutdown even though SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close already shut the same pool down. WHY: Arroyo's normal shutdown sequence calls strategy.close() first and then factory.shutdown(), so the second call to queue.Queue.shutdown raises queue.ShutDown, which is caught and logged as an error. HOW: Make FixedQueuePool.shutdown idempotent by tracking a shutdown flag and returning early on subsequent calls.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.
Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.
Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.
Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.
Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.
The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.
Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.
Claims the committable-offset loop iterates the whole numeric span max_offset - start, burning CPU on large offset gaps every commit cycle.
_get_partition_lock reads and writes partition_locks without a global lock, claimed to let two threads create different locks for one partition and break offset tracking.
States review of queue_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.
States review of result_consumer.py is incomplete with no issue found.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym without a nil guard. WHY: If SiteSetting.default_locale is nil during boot, asset precompilation, or before settings are initialized, every translation lookup raises NoMethodError. HOW: Defensively coerce the default locale with [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.try(:to_sym), :en].compact or a fallback to :en before calling to_sym.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.
Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.
Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.
Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.
Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
I18n.ensure_loaded! reads and initializes @loaded_locales outside LOAD_MUTEX, racing with reload!/load_locale under concurrent requests.
Claims set_locale's `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` (application_controller.rb:159) raises NoMethodError on every request if I18n.fallbacks is not the custom FallbackLocaleList.
FallbackLocaleList subclasses Hash but leaves it empty, so iterating I18n.fallbacks returns nothing.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The Calendar interface now requires a second credentialId argument, but the majority of calendar adapters still implement createEvent(event) with one argument. WHY: With strict: true, this breaks compilation and forces CalendarManager to pass an unused credentialId to adapters that cannot consume it. HOW: Change the interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId?: number): Promise<NewCalendarEventType>;` so existing adapters remain valid and Google can opt-in to the parameter.

WHAT: requestReschedule converts only bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar and never falls back to the user's destinationCalendar. WHY: Unlike handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, and confirm handlers, a booking row without its own destinationCalendar produces an empty array, so calendar operations during reschedule cannot target the organizer's calendar. HOW: Mirror the fallback used elsewhere: `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar] : bookingToReschedule?.user?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule.user.destinationCalendar] : []`.

issues.descricao: Claims GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent dereference an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar is null or empty.
destinationCalendar is defaulted to null in some producers and to an empty array in others.
loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug for dynamic-user bookings, so code reading user.organization gets undefined.

Claims that for references without a credentialId, looping over every calendar reference and deleting each against all user calendar credentials produces duplicate or wrong-target delete calls and errors.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The add_members action splits the comma-separated usernames parameter without trimming whitespace from each value. WHY: A value such as 'alice, bob' causes User.find_by_username(' bob') to return nil, so the user is silently omitted from the group with no feedback. HOW: Strip each username before the lookup, e.g., username.strip inside the loop.

WHAT: group.users.delete(user_id) persists the membership removal immediately, but the action then calls group.save and reports render_json_error if that save fails. WHY: If an unrelated validation causes group.save to fail, the controller returns an error response even though the member has already been removed from the database. HOW: Wrap the deletion and save in a transaction so they succeed or fail atomically, or validate the group before applying the deletion.

WHAT: The addMembers action sends the selected usernames to the server but never clears the usernames property. WHY: Because the input stays populated and the button remains enabled, clicking Add again (or re-selecting the same users) re-submits the same list; the server may then try to add already-existing members and fail on the unique group_users index. HOW: Clear usernames after the server confirms the add, and guard against concurrent submissions.

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.
Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.
Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.
params[:alias_level].present? is false for 0, so choosing the 'nobody' alias level is ignored.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The POST to GitHub’s access-token endpoint only sends `code`, `client_id`, and `client_secret`, omitting `redirect_uri` even though it was included in the authorization request. WHY: GitHub requires the same `redirect_uri` in the token exchange when one was supplied during authorization, so the exchange can be rejected and the installation pipeline will fail. HOW: Add `"redirect_uri": redirect_uri` to the `data` dictionary, reusing the same `redirect_uri` used for the authorize URL.

issues.descricao: Claims the OAuth state is compared to the secret pipeline signature in non-constant time, leaking timing information.
Claims other consumers driving GitHubInstallation without the new OAuth view will always be rejected; no such consumer exists.
Claims a null reference when the github_authenticated_user state is missing; the code only compares it and returns the error page.
test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message, which any error path would produce.
The GitHub OAuth state parameter is compared with != instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information.
The installation sender-login mismatch test asserts only the generic error text, which state mismatch and OAuth failures also produce, so it cannot show the login check caused the rejection.
The OAuth state check in GitHub OAuthLoginView compares the callback state to pipeline.signature with a plain `!=` instead of a constant-time comparison.
Claims the GitHub OAuth token exchange omits redirect_uri, so GitHub returns redirect_uri_mismatch and every installation fails.
Claims a literal 'null' installation_id passes the None check and routes users to the 'Invalid installation request.' page instead of the app installer.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The encoder assumes fixed 2-character session, token, and grant shortcuts, and getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix is not exactly 6 characters. WHY: The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() contract allows 3-letter shortcuts, so a custom grant factory returning a longer shortcut will produce undecodable token IDs. HOW: Validate each grant shortcut length in postInit and reject non-2-character shortcuts at startup.

issues.descricao: Claims setFormParams replaces form params without refreshing the cached grantType, leaving getGrantType() stale.
getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, breaking existing custom grant type factories when the encoder factory calls it.
Token context encoding calls getShouldUseLightweightToken on every token creation, which dereferences the session context client and would NPE where no client is set.
initToken always encodes the token id and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for a grant type without a registered shortcut, so custom or unmapped grants would fail token issuance with a 500.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Recovery codes are persisted as plain-text JSON in credentialData and validated by comparing the raw user input directly to the raw stored codes. WHY: Recovery codes are sensitive single-use credentials; storing and comparing them in plain text exposes them to any party with access to the user-storage backend and violates Keycloak's hashing requirement for this credential type. HOW: In updateCredential, create a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel (which hashes the codes) and persist both its credentialData and secretData; in isValid, hash the input with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode before comparing against the stored hashed codes.

WHAT: Recovery codes are persisted as a JSON array of raw strings in credentialData and validated by direct string equality. WHY: This stores single-factor backup secrets in plaintext, exposing them if the user-storage backend is compromised and bypassing the hashing that the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider uses. HOW: Hash codes with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.hashRawCode before storage and validate with RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.verifyRecoveryCodeInput, matching the local provider's implementation.

issues.descricao: Claims the recovery-code validator uses non-constant-time String.equals, leaking timing information about stored codes.
Claims raw recovery codes are serialized and persisted in cleartext in user storage instead of hashed.
Claims Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without isPresent() can throw NoSuchElementException.
Plaintext recovery codes are serialized and sent to user storage providers via updateCredential, while the local path stores only hashed codes.
Recovery codes are sent to user storage providers in plaintext instead of hashed, so a provider may persist working second-factor codes.
The test user storage accepts any of the user's recovery codes rather than the specific requested code number, unlike the local provider.
BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so it throws NullPointerException for a user missing from the provider's map.
Claims recovery code verification compares hashes with String.equals, enabling timing attacks.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` calls `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, which invokes `useFolder(folderUID)` once per rule. WHY: A rule list with ~80 items will trigger ~80 concurrent folder metadata requests, reintroducing the N+1 loading problem the PR is trying to remove from the ruler path. HOW: Lift folder permission checks to the group/namespace level or cache folder metadata for the list so each rule does not fetch its folder independently.

`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` calls `useFolder` via both `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` and `useCanSilenceInFolder` for every Grafana rule in the list, creating two RTK Query subscriptions per rule. Move folder permission/silence lookups to the group level or memoize by folder UID to keep subscription count proportional to folders, not rules.

issues.descricao: Claims provisioned status now comes from promRule.provenance, which the Prometheus response might omit, making provisioned rules editable.
Claims the promRule prop typed as Rule makes the Grafana prom-rule type guard return false for the GrafanaPromRuleDTO passed by GrafanaRuleListItem.
The menu test asserts exactly 4 menu items although the menuItems map also includes delete, so the count or comment may not match the real menu.
GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only Prometheus rules and drops the ruler matching, so rules being created disappear and rules being deleted show as normal rows with full actions.
The optional chain stops at .rules, so an empty groups array is claimed to call undefined.map() and throw.
The comment says location is redundant, but showLocation={false} is claimed not to be passed, so grouped rules would show the location.
Using promRule.uid as React key could clash if uids are not unique within a group.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The handler looks up the webhook secret with `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without lowercasing the configured header name. WHY: Node.js stores incoming header keys in lowercase, so a CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME value such as "Calcom-Webhook-Secret" will never match and every legitimate request is rejected with 403. HOW: Lowercase the configured header name before indexing, e.g., `(process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret").toLowerCase()`.

WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when parsing fails, so `parsedToken.success` is always true after the call returns. WHY: The `if (!parsedToken.success)` branch that follows in Zoom (and the equivalent branch in Salesforce) is unreachable and gives a false impression of graceful error handling. HOW: Remove the unreachable check, or change parseRefreshTokenResponse to return the SafeParseReturnType without throwing so callers can branch on success.

issues.descricao: Claims the JSDoc describes appData.type as 'the app slug', copied from appData.appId.
Claims the team-credential branch only checks accepted membership instead of admin rights, letting non-admin members create team credentials.
Claims malformed OAuth state makes JSON.parse throw and crash OAuth callbacks with a 500.
Claims the Office365 video adapter passes the wrong app slug 'msteams' to refreshOAuthTokens.
createOAuthAppCredential only verifies team membership, not admin access, before creating a team credential, so any team member can install OAuth apps for the team via a crafted state.
The app-credential webhook decrypts keys with CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY falling back to an empty string when the env var is unset, instead of failing fast.
The app-credential webhook is claimed to accept GET, so a loggable, prefetchable, CSRF-able request carrying the shared secret could overwrite any user's stored OAuth keys.
The app-credential webhook authenticates only by a static shared-secret header, so whoever holds the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials without per-user auth, HMAC or replay protection.
The .env.example tells users to generate CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which is claimed to give only 24 bytes instead of the 32 required by AES256.
The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, so a hanging endpoint could block calendar/video requests.
The truthy userId check treats user id 0 as absent and skips the credential sync endpoint.
Claims decrypted credential keys are stored without validation against the app's credential schema, allowing credential poisoning if the webhook secret is compromised.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container, but the header template still applies the `clearfix` class, whose `::before`/`::after` pseudo-elements use `display: table`. WHY: In a flex formatting context those pseudo-elements become flex items, so they participate in the header layout, create extra gaps before/after the real content, and can be reordered among children because `.panel` and `.extra-info-wrapper` use explicit `order` values. HOW: Remove the `clearfix` class from the `.contents` div in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/header.hbs`, since `.contents` no longer needs float containment.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
Making .small-action a flex container is claimed to make the floated buttons ignore float:right, because they would be flex items, so they collapse next to the description.
Claims that removing the 5px bullet margin in .extra-info-wrapper misaligns category bullets because the wrapper's parent is still float-based and order() has no effect.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The catch block increments retryCount for any error in the whole try body, including after a successful Twilio schedule when only the scheduled=true DB update fails. WHY: A reminder can be retried and eventually deleted while Twilio still holds a scheduled message, causing orphan Twilio messages and lost reminders. HOW: Only increment retryCount when the scheduling call itself fails, and handle DB persistence errors separately.

issues.descricao: Reminders with an empty message or missing phone number never increment retryCount and are re-processed on every cron run until their date passes.
Claims the failed-send branch does not increment retryCount on the success path.
The catch block increments retryCount for any error, including setup failures unrelated to Twilio, which can delete reminders prematurely.
The catch block logs the raw SMS provider error, which may leak phone numbers or message bodies into logs.
